Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the quick intro. Our Legal team reviewed Redwood's standard DPA and has two outstanding asks related to backups and disaster recovery:

1) Backup/DR carve-out: we need explicit language that allows Nova to maintain encrypted backups for disaster recovery beyond the stated deletion window in the DPA, provided those backups are encrypted, access-controlled, and only used for restoration/DR.
2) Retention for litigation hold: if Nova issues a legal hold, we need Redwood to preserve relevant backups for the hold period and notify us of any conflicts.

Please confirm if Redwood can accept a carve-out that permits encrypted backups to be retained up to seven (7) years for DR purposes, with a requirement to isolate and restrict access and to delete earlier if requested and no legal hold exists. If seven years is a hard no, tell us the maximum you can support and whether we can contractually limit access to specific roles.

We'd like to get this wrapped and executed via DocuSign if possible — can you send an updated/redlined DPA and a DocuSign envelope once internal sign-off is complete?

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: DPA: retention & backup carve-outs

Sofia / Karthik — reviewed Elena's ask. High level positions we can take that should be acceptable to Nova while limiting our legal exposure:

1) DR carve-out window: propose a firm 24-month standard window for encrypted backups retained for DR, with the option to negotiate up to 60 months (5 years) for enterprise customers with specific needs. Seven years is unusual for backups; it significantly increases our long-tail risk and complexity for access controls.

2) Access & controls: require that backup copies are encrypted with customer-specific keys (KMS) where possible, and that access to restore operations is logged and limited to a named set of Redwood SRE roles. We should include an obligation to notify Nova within 72 hours if access is requested by any Redwood personnel outside the named roles.

3) Litigation holds: agree to preserve backups subject to Nova's written legal hold notice. Redwood will preserve relevant backup images for the period of the hold and will make commercially reasonable efforts to restore data for eDiscovery. Include a clause requiring Nova to reimburse incremental costs for long-term preservation beyond the negotiated DR window.

4) Subprocessors & transfers: limit cross-border restore operations to jurisdictions approved in the DPA; provide registry of subprocessors and prior notice for any changes affecting restore locations.

Proposed language snippets (summary):
- "Redwood may retain encrypted backup copies for disaster recovery for a period of up to 24 months following deletion from primary systems, unless the Parties agree in writing to a longer period not to exceed 60 months."
- "Redwood will restrict restore access to personnel named in Schedule X and will log all restore events; Redwood will notify Customer within 72 hours of any non-routine restore request."
- "Upon receipt of a written legal hold, Redwood will preserve backup images reasonably necessary for the hold for the duration of the legal hold; Customer will reimburse incremental costs for preservation beyond the agreed DR period."

I attached a short memo that maps these options and the operational trade-offs. If Nova insists on 7 years, we should ask for reimbursement + customer-managed keys + more stringent access controls. Otherwise, try to land at 24-60 months.

Attachment: Legal_Summary_DR_Options.docx

Laura Bennett

Quick operational note from infra/SE perspective:

- We can technically retain encrypted backups per-customer using customer KMS keys for the requested windows. 24 months is straightforward. 60 months is technically feasible but adds cost and increases the number of backup image versions we must track; it will require tagging and a retention schedule in our backup catalog.
- Restore access can be restricted to named SREs; we already support role-based access and restore auditing. We can emit a monthly restore log export to Nova on request.
- If Nova wants 7 years + no-cost preservation, that is a material ask and would push us to an enterprise change order — we should price the incremental storage and operational overhead.

Suggested operational text to include in the DPA redline: "Customer may request extended backup preservation; Redwood will implement extended retention upon execution of a mutually-agreed SOW or fee schedule."

Happy to jump on the call if Legal or Nova want to hammer the exact mechanics.

Elena / Legal Ops — thanks for your patience while we reviewed internally. Please find attached the final redline and a brief summary of the agreed positions. Key points: 

- Agreed baseline DR retention: Redwood will retain encrypted backup copies for up to 24 months for disaster recovery purposes.
- Extended retention: Parties may agree in writing to extended preservation up to 60 months; extended retention beyond 24 months will be subject to a fee schedule (included in the SOW) or Customer-provided KMS keys where required.
- Access & logging: Restore operations will be restricted to named Redwood personnel and logged; Redwood will provide restore logs to Nova on a monthly basis or upon request for eDiscovery.
- Legal hold: Redwood will preserve backup images responsive to a written legal hold for the duration of the hold; Nova will reimburse incremental costs for preservation beyond the agreed DR retention window.
- Subprocessors & transfers: restores that require cross-border transfers will be limited to approved jurisdictions and Redwood will notify Nova in advance of any changes.

Attached: Redlined_DPA_Nova_FINAL.pdf (final redline reflecting above positions)
